title: NeuralProphet for Ordinal Time Series Forecasting: A Two-Stage Approach with Threshold Optimization
content: Air quality indices, severity ratings, and similar series come as ordered categories, yet standard forecasting methods produce continuous predictions. We propose a two-stage approach using NeuralProphet, which decomposes a series into trend, seasonality, and autoregressive components. In the first stage, NeuralProphet is fit to the ordinal labels treated as continuous, yielding a decomposition and a continuous forecast. In the second, ordered thresholds mapping it to categories are optimized on a validation segment, replacing naive rounding. We evaluate on a controlled simulation and two real series, Beijing air quality and electricity load in a Ball State University building. On the simulation, the method recovers the latent ordering and generating components despite being fit on discretized labels, and threshold optimization improves the quadratic weighted kappa over rounding by 0.05 to 0.08, and by more when a miscalibrated trend leaves the ordering intact but the level off. On the real series it leads at every horizon, reaching a kappa of 0.57 on air quality and 0.89 on building load at 72 hours, and the gain grows with the horizon on air quality. The fitted components match each series’ structure. The approach is therefore an effective, interpretable framework for ordinal forecasting without specialized machinery.
